:::{#exm-pois-fitted-totals}
#### Fitted totals for automobile insurance claims

The `Insurance` data distributed with the `MASS` R package [@venables2002modern]
count the automobile insurance claims (`Claims`)
among the policyholders (`Holders`)
in each combination of `District` (4 levels), car `Group`, and driver `Age` (4 levels).
We fit a Poisson regression model for the claim rate per policyholder,
with district and age as categorical covariates
and $\logf{\text{Holders}}$ as the offset:

```{r}
#| label: insurance-fitted-totals
#| code-fold: show
ins <- MASS::Insurance
ins$Age <- factor(ins$Age, ordered = FALSE)
ins_glm <- glm(
  Claims ~ District + Age + offset(log(Holders)),
  family = stats::poisson(),
  data = ins
)
c(observed = sum(ins$Claims), fitted = sum(fitted(ins_glm)))
cbind(
  observed = tapply(ins$Claims, ins$District, sum),
  fitted = tapply(fitted(ins_glm), ins$District, sum)
)
cbind(
  observed = tapply(ins$Claims, ins$Age, sum),
  fitted = tapply(fitted(ins_glm), ins$Age, sum)
)
```

As @thm-pois-fitted-totals guarantees,
the fitted claim counts add up to the 3151 observed claims,
and they also reproduce the observed total in each district and in each age group,
because each non-reference group has an indicator variable in the model,
and each reference group's total is the overall total minus the other groups' totals.
The fitted counts do not match the individual rows, though:

```{r}
#| label: insurance-fitted-rows
#| code-fold: show
head(cbind(ins[c("District", "Age")], observed = ins$Claims,
           fitted = round(fitted(ins_glm), 1)), 4)
```

The first four rows have 38, 35, 20, and 156 observed claims,
but fitted counts of about 38.4, 44.0, 35.6, and 196.9:
the model has no indicator for each row,
so @thm-pois-fitted-totals says nothing about individual rows.
:::
